notation.<a | b>: Required — pick exactly one of the enclosed, pipe-separated alternatives.
notation.[optional]: Optional — the enclosed part may be left out entirely.
Free text supplied by the writer (a name, a place, dialogue, etc.) — never literal.

entries.name: Scene Heading
entries.description: Marks the start of a new scene: where the action happens, and whether it's shot indoors or outdoors. A scene heading must be preceded by a blank line unless it's forced.
entries.howToUse: <INT. | EXT. | INT/EXT. | I/E.> <place> [- time of day]

entries.name: Force Scene Heading
entries.description: Makes any line a scene heading regardless of wording, for non-standard slugs like 'LATER' or 'FLASHBACK' that don't start with INT/EXT.

entries.name: Scene Number
entries.description: Pins an explicit scene number to a heading instead of letting it be numbered automatically in document order. Useful for keeping numbers stable across revisions.

entries.name: Scene Color Tag
entries.description: Tags a scene heading with a color, used by the app to color-code scene cards in an outline or board view.
entries.sceneformNotes: Not part of the Fountain spec. Sceneform reuses the note syntax to carry this, and only recognizes a fixed set of named colors plus hex codes — anything else is treated as an ordinary note, not a color tag.

entries.name: Action
entries.description: Plain descriptive text — what's happening on screen. This is the default for any line that isn't recognized as something more specific.
entries.example: The kettle screams. She doesn't move.

entries.name: Force Action
entries.description: Forces a line to be treated as action even if it would otherwise be read as a character cue or transition — e.g. a short all-caps line that isn't dialogue.

entries.name: Shot
entries.description: Calls out a specific camera shot within a scene, set apart from ordinary action.
entries.example: !!CLOSE ON: the ring, spinning on the counter

entries.name: Character
entries.description: Names who's speaking, right before their dialogue. Detected automatically when an all-caps line sits on its own with dialogue underneath it.

entries.name: Force Character
entries.description: Forces a line to be read as a character cue even if it wouldn't be picked up automatically — e.g. a lowercase or short name.

entries.name: Character Extension
entries.description: A parenthetical note appended to a character cue, most commonly to mark a voice-over, an off-screen line, or that the character is continuing after an interruption.

entries.name: Dual Dialogue
entries.description: Marks two characters speaking at the same time, side by side. The caret goes on the second character's cue; it pairs with the dialogue block immediately above it.
entries.example:
MARIA
Where were you?

JAMES ^
Where were YOU?

entries.name: Dialogue
entries.description: The spoken line(s) following a character cue. Any non-blank line directly under a character cue or parenthetical is read as dialogue.

entries.name: Parenthetical
entries.description: A short direction wedged between a character cue (or a line of dialogue) and the dialogue that follows, e.g. how a line should be delivered.

entries.name: Transition
entries.description: A right-aligned editorial cut, like CUT TO: or FADE OUT. Detected automatically when a standalone all-caps line ends in 'TO:' or matches a known fade/cut phrase.

entries.name: Force Transition
entries.description: Forces a line to be read as a transition even if it doesn't match the automatic 'ends in TO:' pattern.

entries.name: Centered Text
entries.description: Centers a line on the page — commonly used for a single, standalone line like an epigraph or a card.

entries.name: Lyrics
entries.description: Marks a line as sung rather than spoken, typically italicized in output. Works both as its own block and inside a dialogue exchange.

entries.name: Section
entries.description: An outline heading used to organize the script (e.g. by act or sequence) without affecting the printed page. Deeper nesting uses more '#' characters.

entries.name: Synopsis
entries.description: A one-line summary attached to the section or scene above it, used for outlining — never printed on the page.

entries.name: Page Break
entries.description: Forces a new page to start at this point when the script is exported or printed.

entries.name: Title Page Field
entries.description: A key/value field describing the document, written before anything else in the file (Title, Author, Draft date, etc.). A value can continue onto following indented lines.

entries.name: Note
entries.description: An inline comment for the writer's own reference — never printed, never affects scene numbering or structure.

entries.name: Boneyard
entries.description: Comments out a block of text entirely, letting a writer keep an old draft of a scene without it printing or being parsed.

entries.name: Emphasis (Bold / Italic / Underline)
entries.description: Inline text styling inside action or dialogue lines.

entries.name: Paragraph Continuation
entries.description: Keeps two consecutive lines of action or dialogue in the same paragraph instead of splitting them into separate blocks, by leaving exactly two trailing spaces on the otherwise-blank line between them.
entries.sceneformNotes: This two-space continuation rule is specific to Sceneform's engine; other Fountain parsers will typically read the blank line as a normal paragraph break.

entries.name: In-Progress Character Cue
entries.description: While actively typing an all-caps line with nothing under it yet, Sceneform tentatively shows it as a character cue if the cursor is right there — so formatting appears immediately instead of only after dialogue is typed underneath.
entries.howToUse: <NAME> (cursor on this line, nothing below it yet)
entries.sceneformNotes: This is an editor convenience tied to cursor position (the `caretLine` parse option), not a Fountain syntax rule. Once dialogue is typed below, it's just an ordinary character cue.
